chunks: Jamil narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
Regarding a sacrificial animal whose horn is broken, he said: “If the inner horn is sound, then it suffices.”

key_terms.الْأُضْحِيَّةِ: the sacrificial animal offered in ritual sacrifice

ai.seo_question: Does a sacrificial animal with a broken horn still count as valid in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the validity of an uḍḥiyah sacrificial animal when its horn is broken. The ruling states that if the inner horn remains sound, the animal is still sufficient for the sacrifice.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3062 - Jameel narrated from Abu Abdullah (as) regarding a sacrificial animal whose horn is broken.
Imam (as) said: "If the inner horn is intact, it suffices."
